A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe the same PFT/SFDA-PFT research, and their supplied pages are readable. However, v1 refers detailed Aff-Wild2 results to separate supplementary material absent from the supplied PDF, whereas v3 includes Appendices A–E. This limits comparison with that unavailable earlier supplement.

before.justification: v1 reports original subject-level accuracy comparisons on BioVid, StressID and BAH in Tables 2–4, together with feature-size, pairing and embedding analyses.

after.justification: v3 reports original F1 and accuracy comparisons, repeated-seed results, additional backbone evaluations and component ablations in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The core feature translator, frozen source encoder/classifier and cross-entropy, KL and style objectives remain unchanged, including translated-feature cross-entropy in v3 Algorithm 1. Section 5 adds an age-aware pairing variant using younger, expression-matched references for an elderly subject. Renaming PFT to SFDA-PFT and adding pseudocode do not themselves change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate BioVid pain recognition, StressID stress recognition, BAH ambivalence/hesitancy recognition and seven-class Aff-Wild2 expression recognition. Aff-Wild2 was already used in v1. Added backbones, loss variants and analyses of existing older subjects do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The principal benchmark comparator set is retained. The efficiency comparison changes membership: v3 Table 5 adds an entry labeled SFDA-DE and omits DSFDA, SFIT and SFDA-IT from that comparison. The embedding comparison adds SFIT between v1 Figure 6 and v3 Figure 9. SFDA-DE's identity remains unclear because it shares SHOT's citation.

E3.justification: v3 introduces F1 evaluation while retaining accuracy tables in the appendix, changes the stated target-selection protocol from randomly selected to standard fixed subjects, and adds ViT-B/32 and ResNet-50 evaluations. Efficiency reporting changes from time per epoch to adaptation iterations and time per batch. These are reported protocol changes and additions; the unchanged accuracy tables do not establish rerunning those experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's feature-size, pairing and three-model t-SNE analyses, v3 adds loss-component ablations, identity/expression similarity measurements, source-prototype alignment analyses, translated-image examples, backbone robustness tests, style-layer selection, expression-loss comparisons and loss-weight sensitivity studies. Tables 6–7 and 12–19 and Figures 4–5 and 7–10 substantially expand examination of the method's components and behavior.

E5.justification: v3 Section 4.2 first reports three independent BioVid training seeds and F1 of 78.43 ± 0.25%. v1 provides no repeated-run count or uncertainty reporting. This is a limited addition for one method/dataset, not evidence of an increase from a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: v1 Tables 2–4 are numerically retained as v3 Tables 8–10, including PFT accuracies of 82.46%, 79.49% and 62.09%. v3 adds F1 results, full Aff-Wild2 tables within the supplied PDF, backbone results and numerous analysis outcomes. Its opening parameter comparison changes PFT from 0.5M to 5.76M, matching v1 Table 5. New F1 values and differently defined timing results are not same-setting accuracy or speed improvements.

T1.justification: The translator composition and cross-entropy, KL-divergence and feature-moment alignment objectives are mathematically retained. Explicit cross-entropy notation, corrected translator-input notation and pseudocode clarify existing procedures. Neither version provides theorems or proofs, and v3 introduces no substantive formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: neutral-only source-free personalization through expression-preserving feature translation, lower computational cost and strong performance across four FER benchmarks. The rename and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds an age-related interpretation of BioVid failures and an age-aware mitigation, motivates F1 through class imbalance, and expands explanations of expression preservation and image-translation artifacts. It interprets branch similarities and prototype distributions as evidence of specialization and alignment, and backbone experiments as support for broader applicability. These specific interpretations and qualifications were absent from the supplied v1.

D1.justification: v3 adds source/adaptation pseudocode, explicit loss weights, hyperparameter ranges, epoch budgets, preprocessing and augmentation settings, and source-validation selection information. It supplies a stated public code link instead of v1's promised release. Reproducibility remains imperfect: Table 20 specifies source SGD/Nesterov alongside the main text's Adam description, and v3 omits v1's explicit Dlib/68-landmark and demographic pairing details.

R1.justification: v3 adds aging-related references by Guo et al., Sönmez and Kim et al., plus Zeeshan et al.'s MUSACO work, and removes the Dlib reference. These support limited extensions concerning age and personalization; the main positioning against model-based SFDA and image translation remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites the training/adaptation explanations and results discussion, reorganizes the main evaluation around F1, and moves original dataset descriptions and accuracy comparisons into Appendix C. It restructures the ablation narrative and introduces a numbered appendix hierarchy. Terminology, author information and conference headers also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column to a single-column layout. The opening diagram is redrawn and merged with a bar-chart replacement for v1 Table 1; pairing examples and aggregate results are combined; accuracy tables relocate to the appendix; and numerous tables, histograms, plots and algorithm displays are added. Figure 10 introduces a caption error that reverses the plotted loss-weight axes.

improvement.justification: Direct loss ablations, additional backbones, F1 reporting, a three-seed check and expanded implementation information strengthen validation and reproducibility beyond v1. The net gain is limited by new inconsistencies: Appendix C.2 gives 71.49% StressID accuracy and describes an Aff-Wild2 deficit, contradicting Tables 9 and 11; optimizer descriptions conflict; and Figure 10 reverses its axis descriptions. These errors weaken the reliability and clarity of otherwise useful additions.
